vedicSutras.name: Criss-Cross Multiplication (Urdhva Tiryagbhyam)
steps: Step 1: Multiply unit digits vertically: (Units × Units)
Step 2: Cross multiply outer and inner pairs and add with carry: (Tens × Units + Units × Tens)
Step 3: Multiply tens digits vertically: (Tens × Tens) + carry
vedicSutras.timeSaved: 15 seconds vs standard school long multiplication

vedicSutras.name: Base 100 / 1000 Multiplication (Nikhilam Navatashcaramam)
steps: Step 1: Write deviations from 100/1000: (e.g. 96 is -4, 93 is -7)
Step 2: Right side = Product of deviations: (-4) × (-7) = 28
Step 3: Left side = Cross add either number with other's deviation: (96 - 7) = 89
Step 4: Combine = 8928!
vedicSutras.walkthrough: Deviations: +6 and +8. Right side: 6 × 8 = 48. Left side: 106 + 8 = 114. Combine: 11448 in 3 seconds!

vedicSutras.name: Squaring Numbers Ending in 5 (Ekadhikena Purvena)
steps: Step 1: Last two digits are ALWAYS 25 (since 5² = 25)
Step 2: Multiply the preceding number (n) by its successor (n + 1)
Step 3: Prepend n × (n+1) before 25
vedicSutras.walkthrough: Preceding number = 7. Next integer = 8. 7 × 8 = 56. Tack on 25 ⇒ 5625 in 2 seconds!

vedicSutras.name: Proportional Sub-Base Multiplication (Anurupyena)
steps: Step 1: Determine working base and its ratio to primary base 100 or 1000
Step 2: Calculate deviations and cross-add as in Nikhilam
Step 3: Multiply or divide cross-sum by the sub-base ratio before combining with deviation product
vedicSutras.walkthrough: Deviations from 50: -2 and -4. Cross-add: 48 - 4 = 44. Divide by 2: 44 / 2 = 22. Deviations product: (-2) × (-4) = 08. Answer = 2208!

vedicSutras.name: Vinculum Method (Negative Digits / Bar Numbers)
vedicSutras.suitability: Numbers containing large digits (6, 7, 8, 9) to eliminate carries
steps: Step 1: Convert digits > 5 into negative digits (10 - d with bar)
Step 2: Add 1 carry to the previous left digit
Step 3: Perform multiplication using only small tables (1 to 5) with zero carries

vedicSutras.name: Beejank / Digital Root 3-Second Option Eliminator
vedicSutras.suitability: Option elimination in Bank Prelims Simplification, Arithmetic & Multiplication
steps: Step 1: Compute digit sum of each number in the equation, casting out 9s
Step 2: Apply the arithmetic operation (+, −, ×) on single-digit Beejanks
Step 3: Only the option with matching Beejank can be correct; eliminate others instantly
vedicSutras.walkthrough: Beejank of 487: 4+8+7 = 19 → 1+9 = 1. Beejank of 69: 6+9 = 15 → 6. Product Beejank: 1 × 6 = 6. Check options: only 33,603 has digit sum 6 (3+3+6+0+3 = 15 → 6)!

vedicSutras.name: Transpose and Apply (Paravartya Yojayet)
vedicSutras.suitability: Mental division when divisor is close to powers of 10 (89, 97, 103, 112)
steps: Step 1: Find divisor deviation from base
Step 2: Transpose (invert) the sign of the deviation
Step 3: Perform synthetic mental addition with transposed digits to drop quotient and remainder
vedicSutras.walkthrough: Divisor 89 has deviation -11. Transpose: +11. Quotient = 13, Remainder = 77 in 5 seconds without scratch work!

shortcuts.title: M. Tyra's Universal Alligation Cross Method
shortcuts.book: Magical Book on Quicker Maths - M. Tyra
shortcuts.normalMethod: Set up algebraic equations with x and y: c₁x + c₂y = cₘ(x + y) and solve.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Place cheaper (C) and dearer (D) at top corners, mean (M) at center. Cross difference gives the exact ratio: (D - M) : (M - C).
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Conservation of total value: x(M - C) = y(D - M).
shortcuts.example: Mix tea at ₹60/kg and ₹85/kg to get average of ₹75/kg.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Mixing Cost Price with Selling Price. If one value has profit, convert it to pure Cost Price first!

shortcuts.title: M. Tyra's 2-Year and 3-Year CI-SI Difference Formulas
shortcuts.book: Magical Book on Quicker Maths - M. Tyra
shortcuts.normalMethod: Calculate 2 years SI = 2PR/100, calculate 2 years CI = P(1+R/100)² - P, then subtract.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Use direct formula: Diff₂ = P × (R/100)² for 2 years. Diff₃ = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100) for 3 years.
shortcuts.whyItWorks: The second year interest difference is purely the simple interest earned on the first year's interest: (PR/100) × (R/100).
shortcuts.example: Diff between CI and SI on ₹5,000 for 2 years at 12% p.a.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Using this 2-year formula when compounding is half-yearly (which converts 2 years into 4 compounding cycles).

shortcuts.title: M. Tyra's Relative Speed Train Crossing Rule
shortcuts.book: Magical Book on Quicker Maths - M. Tyra
shortcuts.normalMethod: Set up distance equation with relative speeds, convert km/h to m/s separately.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Time = (L₁ + L₂) / (S₁ ± S₂). If opposite direction, add speeds; if same direction, subtract speeds. Multiply km/h by 5/18 in one step.
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Total length to cover is always the sum of both lengths regardless of direction.
shortcuts.example: Trains 140m and 160m travel in opposite directions at 42 km/h and 30 km/h.
shortcuts.topperSteps: Relative Speed = 42 + 30 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Total Length = 300m. Time = 300 / 20 = 15s in 4 seconds!
shortcuts.commonMistake: Subtracting lengths when trains move in the same direction. Lengths ALWAYS add!

shortcuts.title: Rajesh Verma's Duplex Method for Squaring
shortcuts.book: Fast Track Objective Arithmetic - Rajesh Verma
shortcuts.normalMethod: Multiply number by itself using standard 2-line or 3-line multiplication.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Compute Duplex terms: (ab)² = D(a) | D(ab) | D(b) = a² | 2ab | b² with column carry.
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Direct algebraic expansion of (10a + b)² = 100a² + 20ab + b².
shortcuts.commonMistake: Forgetting to double the product for 2-digit duplex (it is 2ab, not ab).

shortcuts.title: Rajesh Verma's Successive Percentage Formula
shortcuts.book: Fast Track Objective Arithmetic - Rajesh Verma
shortcuts.normalMethod: Assume 100, calculate first change, then apply second change on intermediate result.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Net Change% = A + B + (A × B) / 100. (Use negative sign for decreases or discounts).
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Compounding factor: (1 + A/100)(1 + B/100) = 1 + (A + B + AB/100)/100.
shortcuts.example: Price increases by 25% then decreases by 20%.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Ignoring the sign of B when it is a reduction or discount.

shortcuts.title: R.S. Aggarwal's Unit Digit Power Cyclicity Law
shortcuts.topperMethod: Powers of 2, 3, 7, 8 have cyclicity 4. Divide power by 4. If remainder is r, unit digit is dʳ (if r=0, use d⁴). Powers of 4, 9 have cyclicity 2. Powers of 0, 1, 5, 6 never change!
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Modular arithmetic modulo 10 guarantees periodic repetition in power unit digits.
shortcuts.topperSteps: 67 mod 4 = 3. Unit digit of 3³ is 7! Solved in 2 seconds.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Taking remainder 0 as power 0 instead of power 4.

shortcuts.title: Shantanu Shukla's Quadratic Sign-Flip 5-Second Rule
shortcuts.book: Daksh Quant Speed Math - Shantanu Shukla
shortcuts.normalMethod: Factorize both equations into roots, solve both, and compare all 4 pairs.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Inspect equation signs first: If signs are (-, +) roots are (+, +). If (+, +) roots are (-, -). If both constants are negative, choose CND immediately!
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Roots of a quadratic with negative constant term have opposite signs (+ and -). Two equations each having one positive and one negative root overlap, making a strict inequality impossible.
shortcuts.normalSteps: Calculate roots for x (+17, -3) and roots for y (+21, -2), then cross-compare. Takes 45s.
shortcuts.topperSteps: Both c < 0 (constant terms -51 and -42 are negative). Mark 'CND / No relation' immediately in 3 seconds!
shortcuts.commonMistake: Forgetting that leading coefficients (a and d) must be divided out when roots are calculated.

shortcuts.title: Shantanu Shukla's Percentage Split & Interchange Law
shortcuts.book: Daksh Quant Speed Math - Shantanu Shukla
shortcuts.normalMethod: Multiply fraction by base and do floating point division.
shortcuts.topperMethod: 1) Use x% of y = y% of x. 2) Break awkward percentages into 50% ± 10% ± 1% ± 0.5%.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Struggling with the decimal when 250% is simply 2 + 1/2 of the number.

shortcuts.title: Sumit Sir's Ratio Method for Compound Interest
shortcuts.book: PW Banking Game Changer - Sumit Sir
shortcuts.normalMethod: Use formula A = P(1 + R/100)ᵗ, expand polynomials and solve large decimals.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Convert rate to fraction 1/x. Principal : Amount for t years = xᵗ : (x + 1)ᵗ. CI is the unit difference.
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Compound interest is exponential scaling of the fractional growth factor.
shortcuts.example: P = ₹8,000, R = 15% (3/20), Time = 2 years. Find CI.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Squaring the interest instead of the base ratio.

shortcuts.title: Sumit Sir's Mixture Replacement Formula
shortcuts.book: PW Banking Game Changer - Sumit Sir
shortcuts.normalMethod: Recalculate remaining volume and added water step-by-step for each replacement round.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Remaining Pure Liquid = Initial Volume × [1 - (Replaced Volume / Total Capacity)]ⁿ.
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Each replacement removes an identical fraction of the currently remaining pure liquid.
shortcuts.example: A vessel has 60L pure milk. 12L is taken out and replaced with water. Repeated 2 times total.
shortcuts.normalSteps: Round 1: 48L milk. Round 2: 12 × 48/60 = 9.6L milk removed, 48 - 9.6 = 38.4L milk left. Takes 40s.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Confusing remaining pure liquid with the amount of water in the final mixture.
